review_notes: אַרְצָה's directive he is Sd, not a paragogic he, so it takes the *upon* the ASV writes for it rather than going unrepresented (rule 32).

review_notes: Variant WLC.JOB.1.21.v003 is underdetermined and the projection's base reading of s004 is compatible with the ASV; no textual decision is made here (rule 9).
*out of* is taken as מִן's own multi-word preposition (rule 24), leaving יָצָא the bare *came I*.

variant_decisions.evidence: Qere יָצָאתִי and ketiv יצתי are plene and defective spellings of the same first-person perfect of יצא; the ASV's 'Naked came I out of my mother's womb' renders both alike and no ASV note is mapped to this unit. The English cannot distinguish the spellings, so both readings are retained and the qere base fallback carries the projection.

alignments.note: לֹא → *not*; the ASV writes it after the verb, and the unit is discontinuous under rule 25.
Waw plus negative fused into the single word *nor*, headed on the negative, which is what distinguishes it from a bare *and* (rule 35).
The ASV recasts לֵאלֹהִים as a bare English object, *charged God*, leaving the preposition nothing (rule 40).
תִּפְלָה rendered adverbially as *foolishly* (the ASV's margin gives the nominal reading).

review_notes: וְלֹא is the ordinary rule 35 fusion into *nor*, headed on the negative.
לְ before אֱלֹהִים goes unrepresented because the ASV writes the object bare (rule 40).
